How to Make Your Website Appear in ChatGPT, Gemini, and AI Search

AI SearchChatGPT SEOGemini SearchGEOGenerative Engine OptimizationWebsite VisibilityDigital MarketingSEO StrategyAI MarketingSearch Engine Optimization
Webcore Solutions10 min read

Something significant is happening to the way people search for information online, and most business owners have not caught up with it yet.

For the past two decades, getting found online meant one thing: ranking on Google. You optimised your pages, built backlinks, and chased that first-page position. That still matters. But it is no longer the whole picture.

Today, a growing number of people are skipping the search results page entirely. They are typing their questions directly into ChatGPT, asking Google's Gemini for recommendations, or using AI-powered search tools like Perplexity to get instant, conversational answers. And here is the part that should get your attention: those AI tools are recommending specific businesses, products, and websites in their responses.

The question is whether yours is one of them.

This guide explains exactly how AI search works, why it matters for your business, and what you can do right now to make sure your website shows up when it counts.

Why AI Search Is Different From Traditional SEO

When someone searches on Google, they get a list of links and they choose which one to click. They are in control of the journey.

When someone asks ChatGPT or Gemini a question, they get a direct answer. The AI has already done the filtering. It has decided which sources are credible, which information is relevant, and which businesses are worth mentioning and it presents all of that as a single, confident response.

This is a fundamental shift. In traditional search, you compete for clicks. In AI search, you compete to be cited.

If the AI does not know your website exists, or does not consider it credible enough to reference, you will not appear in the answer. The user will never see your business. And unlike a Google results page where you might appear on page two, there is no page two in an AI response. You are either in it or you are not.

This new discipline has a name. It is called Generative Engine Optimisation, or GEO, and it is quickly becoming one of the most important things a business can invest in.

How AI Tools Decide What to Recommend

Before you can optimise for AI search, you need to understand how these systems work.

ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and similar tools are trained on enormous amounts of text from across the internet. They learn which sources are authoritative, which content is accurate, and which businesses are consistently mentioned in the context of specific topics. When a user asks a question, the AI draws on all of that training to construct its answer and it tends to reference sources it has seen mentioned repeatedly, across multiple credible contexts.

There are also tools like Perplexity and the newer versions of ChatGPT that actively browse the web in real time. These tools pull from live websites when forming their answers, which means your current website content, your recent articles, and your structured data all play a direct role in whether you get cited.

The practical takeaway is this: AI tools favour websites that are authoritative, well-structured, clearly written, and consistently referenced by other credible sources. Sound familiar? These are the same foundations of good traditional SEO but with some important differences in how you apply them.

Step 1: Write Content That Directly Answers Real Questions

AI search is built around questions. People ask AI tools things like "what is the best web design agency for small businesses" or "which accounting software is easiest to use" or "how do I protect my business website from hackers." The AI scans its training data and the live web for content that most directly and clearly answers those questions.

If your website content is vague, overly promotional, or structured around keywords rather than genuine answers, AI tools will pass it over in favour of content that actually helps the person asking.

The fix is straightforward. Think about the ten most common questions your customers ask before they hire you or buy from you. Write a dedicated piece of content that answers each one thoroughly, clearly, and in plain language. Do not bury the answer in paragraphs of preamble get to it quickly, then expand.

Blog posts, FAQ pages, and resource guides are particularly effective for this. They signal to AI tools that your website is a source of useful information, not just a sales brochure.

Step 2: Build Genuine Authority in Your Niche

AI systems learn who the authorities are in any given field by looking at who gets mentioned, cited, and linked to across the web. If your business is regularly referenced in industry publications, featured in relevant blog posts, and recommended in community discussions, the AI starts to associate your brand with credibility in your space.

This means your off-site presence matters just as much as your on-site content.

Reach out to industry blogs and publications and offer to contribute articles or be featured as an expert source. Get your business listed and reviewed on reputable directories relevant to your industry. Build genuine backlinks from websites that your target audience actually reads and trusts. When other credible sources reference you, AI systems pick up on that pattern.

Think of it this way: the AI is asking itself, "Who do people trust in this space?" Your job is to make sure the answer points to you.

Step 3: Make Sure Your Website Is Crystal Clear About What You Do

This sounds obvious, but it is where a surprising number of business websites fall short.

AI tools need to understand immediately what your business does, who you serve, and where you operate. If your homepage is heavy on clever taglines and light on clear information, the AI will struggle to categorise you accurately and a source it cannot categorise clearly is a source it will not cite confidently.

Your homepage should state plainly what your business does, who it is for, and what makes it different. Your about page should give genuine context about your team, your experience, and your background. Your service or product pages should be specific and detailed, not padded with filler content.

Also make sure your business name, address, phone number, and website are consistent across every platform where you appear your Google Business Profile, your social media accounts, your directory listings, and your website itself. AI tools cross-reference this information when assessing whether a business is legitimate and established.

Step 4: Use Structured Data to Help AI Understand Your Content

Structured data is a way of labelling your website content so that search engines and AI tools can understand exactly what type of information each part of your site contains. It is written in a format called Schema markup and it sits in the background of your website, invisible to visitors but very visible to crawlers and AI systems.

For a business website, the most important structured data types are your business name, location, contact details, opening hours, services offered, and customer reviews. For a blog or resource section, article schema tells AI tools that a piece of content is an informational article, who wrote it, when it was published, and what it covers.

If your website runs on WordPress, a plugin like Rank Math or Yoast SEO makes adding structured data straightforward without needing to touch any code. If you have a custom-built site, ask your developer to implement Schema markup for your key pages.

This is one of the most underused advantages available to business websites right now. Most sites do not have it properly implemented, which means adding it puts you ahead of the majority of your competitors in AI visibility.

Step 5: Get Your Business Mentioned Across the Web

Repeat appearances matter enormously in AI search. When an AI tool sees your business name, your website, and your area of expertise mentioned consistently across multiple sources articles, reviews, forums, social media, directories it builds a picture of you as an established and trusted presence in your field.

Start with the basics. Claim and fully complete your Google Business Profile. Get listed on industry-specific directories that your customers actually use. Encourage satisfied customers to leave reviews on Google, Trustpilot, and any other review platforms relevant to your industry. Reviews are not just social proof for humans they are data points that AI tools use to assess the credibility and reputation of a business.

Then go further. Participate genuinely in online communities where your target audience asks questions Reddit threads, LinkedIn groups, Quora topics, niche forums. Answer questions helpfully, without being promotional. When you are a visible and helpful presence in the conversations your customers are having, AI tools trained on that content start to recognise your authority in those conversations.

Step 6: Keep Your Content Fresh and Current

AI tools that browse the web in real time like Perplexity and the browsing-enabled version of ChatGPT give preference to content that is current and regularly updated. A blog post published three years ago and never touched again is a less attractive citation than one that has been reviewed and updated recently.

Make a habit of auditing your existing content every six months. Update statistics, refresh examples, and add any new information that is relevant. Add the date of the last update to your articles so AI tools can see at a glance that the content is current.

Publishing new content consistently also signals that your website is active and relevant. You do not need to publish every day. One genuinely useful, well-written piece per week is worth far more than five rushed posts that add nothing.

Step 7: Be Genuinely Quotable

Here is something most SEO guides do not talk about: AI tools love a clear, well-expressed insight that they can pull directly into a response.

When you write content, aim to include at least a few sentences that are crisp, definitive, and quotable. A clear statement of fact, a well-framed piece of advice, a direct answer to a common question expressed in a single memorable sentence. These are the kinds of lines that AI tools lift and include in their answers, often with a citation back to your site.

Think about how journalists write. They work quotes into their stories because a well-expressed thought communicates more than a paragraph of explanation. Apply the same thinking to your content, and you give AI tools something worth citing.

The Bottom Line

AI search is not replacing traditional SEO overnight. Google is still the dominant search engine and optimising for it still matters. But the trajectory is clear. More people are using AI tools to find recommendations, get advice, and discover businesses and that number is growing every month.

The businesses that appear in those AI responses will have a significant advantage over those that do not. And the gap between those two groups is widening right now, in real time, as you read this.

The good news is that most of what makes a website visible to AI tools is the same thing that makes it genuinely useful to the people it is trying to serve: clear information, real expertise, honest answers, and a consistent presence across the web. There is no shortcut. There is just the work of building a website and a brand that deserves to be recommended.

Start that work today, and the AI tools will start to notice.
